routine.heading: How the book builds skills
routine.intro: The pages follow the order little hands learn best, from warm-up lines to a certificate at the end.

steps.title: Warm up
steps.body: Two pages of lines from a green dot to a star build the hand muscles for writing.

steps.title: Learn
steps.body: Color the big letter, number or shape, then trace the gray ones on real writing lines.

steps.title: Draw
steps.body: Draw a cat, house, fish, flower and robot in 4 easy steps, then try each one on your own.

steps.title: Play
steps.body: Match letters, find missing ones, count, spot patterns and solve mazes, then earn the Super Star certificate.

items.name: Letters A to Z, uppercase and lowercase
Shapes: circle, square, triangle, rectangle, oval, star, heart, diamond
Step-by-step drawing: cat, house, fish, flower, robot
Letter games: match, find, missing letters, first sounds
Number games: count and circle, number match
Shape and logic puzzles: find the shape, odd one out, what’s next

tips.heading: Tips for grown-ups, straight from page 3
items: Do 1 or 2 pages a day. Short and happy is best!
Start with the warm-up lines to build little hand muscles.
Trace with a crayon or a fat pencil.
Start each letter at the top and go down.
Say the letter name and sound: “C says /k/ like cat.”
Praise trying, not perfect lines. Every wobble counts!
Print extra copies of favorite pages to practice again.

items.name: Letters and sounds
items.body: Every letter in uppercase and lowercase, each paired with a picture word like apple, ball and cat.

items.name: Numbers and counting
items.body: Writing 1 to 9, counting objects, and matching numbers to dots.

items.name: Shapes
items.body: Tracing 8 shapes, writing their names and finding them among look-alikes.

items.name: Pencil control and drawing
items.body: Warm-up lines, dotted tracing and 5 step-by-step drawings that build a steady hand.

items.name: Thinking skills
items.body: Patterns, odd one out, missing letters and mazes that stretch attention and problem solving.

faq.q: What paper and printer do I need?
faq.a: Any home printer. Pages are US Letter size (8.5 × 11 in) and also print on A4 with “fit to page”. Thicker paper holds up better to crayons and markers.

faq.q: Is it right for my child?
faq.a: It’s made for preschool and kindergarten, ages 3 to 6. Younger learners can color and trace; older ones can say each sound, write the missing letters and solve the puzzles.

products.tagline: Look, find and escape! Sharp eyes, busy minds.
highlights: ABC and 123 path mazes, plus a Super Finder certificate

routine.heading: How the book builds skills
routine.intro: Pages get harder as the book goes on, so there’s always a next challenge. Skip around and pick what your child enjoys.

steps.title: Hunt
steps.body: Say the target letter or number together, color every match, then count how many you found.

steps.title: Find
steps.body: In 26 busy A to Z scenes, point to each little picture, say its first sound, then find it in the big scene.

steps.title: Spot
steps.body: Circle every matching shape, then find the animals whose names start with the letter of the page.

steps.title: Escape
steps.body: Solve mazes in 4 levels and follow ABC and 123 paths, then earn the Super Finder certificate.

items.name: Letter hunts: color every match, then count
A to Z picture hunts in busy scenes
Shape Spy: circles, squares, triangles, stars, hearts, ovals, rectangles, diamonds
First Letter Fun: animals by first letter
Letter Challenge: no names, just sounds

tips.heading: Tips for grown-ups, straight from page 3
items: Pages get harder as the book goes on. Skip around and pick what your child enjoys.
Letter and number hunts: say the target’s name together, color each match, then count.
A to Z picture hunts: point to each little picture, say the word and its first sound, then find it in the big scene.
Shape Spy: circle every matching shape, then count them out loud.
First letter pages: say each animal’s name slowly and listen for the first sound.
Mazes: trace with a finger first, then with a crayon.
Finish the book to earn the Super Finder certificate!

items.name: Letters and first sounds
items.body: Spotting uppercase and lowercase letters, and hearing the first sound in words like apple, ant and anchor.

items.name: Numbers and counting
items.body: Finding every matching number, counting how many, and following 1 to 20 in order.

items.name: Shapes
items.body: Picking out 8 shapes among look-alikes and counting them out loud.

items.name: Visual attention
items.body: Searching busy scenes for small details, a skill that supports early reading.

items.name: Problem solving
items.body: Mazes in 4 levels plus ABC and 123 paths that build planning and patience.

faq.q: What paper and printer do I need?
faq.a: Any home printer. Pages are US Letter size (8.5 × 11 in) and also print on A4 with “fit to page”. The picture hunts are in full color, so a color printer shows them best.

faq.q: Which book should we start with?
faq.a: Both are for ages 3 to 6. ABC, 123 & Shapes teaches letters, numbers and shapes through tracing and drawing. Find It! practices the same skills through searching, counting and mazes, so it works as a next step or alongside it.

faq.q: Is it too hard for a 3-year-old?
faq.a: Pages get harder as the book goes on. Younger children can start with the letter hunts, Shape Spy and Level 1 mazes, and come back to the harder pages later.
